name: Clarington Connector

values.DataCenterNotes: The federal energy data release says the line would move Marcellus and Utica gas into Ohio for data center and power demand.

researcher_notes: EQT is building a new line called the Clarington Connector. EQT raised its size from 300 to 400 million cubic feet a day on its fourth quarter 2025 earnings call, as reported by RBN Energy and Natural Gas Intelligence in February 2026. The August 2026 release of the federal Energy Information Administration project list (sheet Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, Excel row 26) names the project, lists EQT Corp, announced, intrastate, in service 2028, 400 million cubic feet a day, and says it would move gas into Ohio for data center and power demand. That is the data center tie. It is not a named campus or customer. Rule 8 applies, so endpoints are not needed. It is a new line, not an existing row. It is not the Borealis row P7794 (Texas Gas Transmission, 265 miles, 2 billion cubic feet a day, Clarington to Lebanon), not the TEMAX row P2008 (Texas Eastern, Clarington to Delta), and not the Ohio Valley Connector rows P6897 (Equitrans, 50 miles, 850 million cubic feet a day, operating) or P4454 (an operating 350 million cubic feet a day expansion of the same Ohio Valley Connector). No existing row carries the Clarington Connector name or EQT as owner for this line. Start state is Ohio. The end state is left blank because sources disagree. The Natural Gas Intelligence map caption says the route links the EQT system in Belmont and Monroe counties, Ohio, to Marshall County, West Virginia. The federal list says Ohio and Pennsylvania. The article bodies are behind paywalls, so only the captions and headlines were read. Length, diameter, cost, permit and exact route were not found. Dates conflict: RBN says end of 2026 and the federal list says 2028. The Pipeline and Gas Journal article from February 2026 places the line in EQT's growth budget but states no data center tie. The owner spelling EQT Corp matches the ownership team's style; no existing entity was found. A prior run held this as monitor under the old rules and the new data center rules now make it a new row. Confidence is medium because the only data center wording is the federal list note.
